Commit message:
switch remaining tests away from fakeAsync (#33889)

Reworks most of the remaining `fakeAsync` tests in the CDK and Material. The tests that assert on
errors reported asynchronously (e.g. thrown from an RxJS subscription) now use
`jasmine.spyOnGlobalErrorsAsync`.

The `material/list` test was failing without `fakeAsync` because the initial `ngModel` value from
`beforeEach` was written at the test's first `await`, clearing the selection. We now flush it before
the test starts.

Also fixes a `cdk/table` test that was detecting changes on the wrong fixture.

A list column that allows null elements is now written `T?[]`.

@noCheck(elementNotNull)`. It typed `tags` as `string[]` while the

Commit message:
bundle the manifest into git-hosted store-index rows (#17369)

The git fetchers wrote store-index rows with no bundled manifest, so the
warm prefetch re-derived `requiresBuild` from the row's files on every
install, reading and parsing `package.json` once per git dependency, and
the cached git prepare check could read it again.

`queue_files_index` now reads the manifest once, derives `requiresBuild`
from it and the file list, and stores the normalized manifest in the row,
as pnpm v11 does. Rows with a bundled manifest keep their stored
`requiresBuild`; only rows written by older releases are re-derived.

Commit message:
clear the sse maxDurationMs timer when the subscription ends (#7666)

Related to #7663

## 🎯 Changes

With `sse.maxDurationMs` set, `resolveResponse` starts a timer for each
subscription and only clears it when the request signal aborts. If the
signal never aborts, the timer stays pending for the full
`maxDurationMs` and keeps its closure and the event loop alive. That
happens when:

- the generator returns
- the procedure throws before streaming (e.g. in a middleware)
- the response body is cancelled
- `responseMeta` throws while the SSE response is being built
- the SSE stream errors (e.g. `onError` throws while an error is being
formatted)

Commit message:
respect `dir` of ancestor elements throughout components (#31459)

Issue number: internal

---------

## What is the current behavior?

Some components check `document.dir === 'rtl'` to determine whether to
be left-to-right or right-to-left.

## What is the new behavior?

- Components consistently use `isRTL(this.el)`. This way, any element in
the parent chain can define RTL, not just the root document element.
- The host element is a required parameter to `isRTL`.

## Does this introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [X] No

Commit message:
publish through npm trusted publishing (#1560)

The release job authenticates to npm through OIDC: it gets `id-token: write` and no
`npm-token`, and `actions/setup-node` no longer takes `registry-url`, whose placeholder
`_authToken` in `.npmrc` would shadow the OIDC flow. pnpm 12 exchanges the token itself,
and the npm of Node.js 26 from `.tool-versions` is newer than the 11.5.1 that trusted
publishing needs. The release job lists `contents: write` too, since a job with
permissions gets no others.

Commit message:
count UTF-16 lengths with `simd-utf16-len` (#11259)

Replaces the char-by-char UTF-16 length loops in `string_wizard` and
`rolldown_error` with
[`simd-utf16-len`](https://github.com/SyMind/simd-utf16-len), and counts
newlines in the diagnostic locators with `memchr`.

Speedup over `main` on an M3 Max. Inputs are `typescript.js` (ascii), a
vitepress dist chunk (mixed, 3% non-ASCII bytes), and TypeScript's zh-cn
`diagnosticMessages.generated.json` (cjk). Ranges cover an edit every 64
KB and every 512 B. Pure-ASCII `source_map` barely moves because it
already had an `is_ascii` fast path.

| | ascii (9.1 MB) | mixed (1.3 MB) | cjk (0.3 MB) |
|---|--
